A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAG-MoE study. All 11 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and references, support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, model ablations and expert-routing analyses in Tables 1–4 and Figure 6, plus a 65-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, expert-routing analyses and user-study outcomes reported in v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4.1 retain the same hierarchical task annotation, routing-signature aggregation, predictive alignment loss and inference-time prompt rewriting. The architecture still uses four experts with top-1 routing in the final ten transformer blocks.

E1.justification: The training-data sources and task coverage are unchanged. Evaluation still uses ICE-Bench, EmuEdit-Bench, GEdit-Bench, DreamBench++ and OmniContext, with the same qualitative scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and the qualitative comparisons. UNO already appears in v1's Table 3 and Figure 5; supplying its missing citation in v2 does not introduce a new baseline.

E3.justification: The reported model settings, evaluation metrics, normalization and comparison procedures remain unchanged. Both versions describe the same user study with 65 participants, 50 ICE-Bench cases and 350 evaluated sets.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same dense-model and alignment-loss ablations. Figure 6 redisplays the existing convergence curves and backpack-editing expert-specialization analysis; no analytical question or experiment is added.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the existing loss curves and user-preference percentages are retained.

E6.justification: All entries and numerical values in Tables 1–4 match, as do the qualitative outcomes and user-study percentages. For example, TAG-MoE's ICE-Bench vllmqa remains 0.852, and its EmuEdit/GEdit vllmqa scores remain 0.9284/0.8854. Figure 6 rearranges existing results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), defining the MoE output, semantic embedding, routing signature and training losses, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, mathematical arguments or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: task-aware routing through hierarchical semantic supervision, reduced task interference and strong performance across five benchmarks.

C2.justification: The explanations of cross-task benefits, expert specialization and baseline failures are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitation concerning joint instruction-image understanding and the same proposed multimodal-reasoning direction.

D1.justification: The dataset-construction pipeline, implementation details and project-page link are unchanged. No additional hyperparameters, hardware specifications, training-time information or code/data access instructions are supplied.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 45 to 58 entries, adding works such as Re-Align, DreamBooth and KV-Edit, and supplying UNO's missing reference. These are mainly additions to citation groups; the related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial updates affect citation callouts, including replacing UNO's unresolved citation, and the arXiv version/date stamp. The prose, terminology, section sequence and narrative structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 moves from a single-column display on page 8 to a larger, full-width display on page 9. Its panels are rearranged, the source image becomes repeated insets, and the material-editing heatmap rows are reordered. Table 4 and subsequent content reflow without substantive changes to their displays.

improvement.justification: The enlarged Figure 6 makes the existing loss curves and expert-routing evidence easier to inspect, while resolving UNO's missing citation improves attribution. These provide limited presentation benefits; the scientific results, methodological support, reproducibility details and stated limitations remain unchanged.
